apps.name: Nova Launcher
apps.whats_new: New in 3.53 — Entertainment this week: your weekly entertainment budget now lives in the Launcher itself, in the My Balance section, and works fully offline — no chat Nova, no network, no Gemini needed. The weekly number is worked out on the phone from your stored budget figures (defaults are your November numbers: $1,735 income, $457 rent, $25 phone, $35 subscriptions, $165 Uber float reserve, $300 essentials, $50 buffer — a $703 monthly pool, $162 a week), and every figure is changeable right on the card. Weeks start Monday: go over one week and the overage comes off next week's number automatically, and a bigger debt keeps rolling until it's paid down. Nova logs what she buys for you automatically — a completed Dunkin order counts against the budget the moment it goes through and the report says how much is left; Walmart groceries and Uber rides do NOT count. You can also tell her a spend yourself ("I spent $20 on entertainment"), ask "entertainment budget" any time, or pin one week by saying "set this week's entertainment budget to $100" — the pin ends Monday. Anything Nova didn't buy is caught by the Monday bank sweep in chat.

apps.name: Nova Voice
apps.whats_new: Engine registration fix: Nova Voice now answers Android's engine-data checks (voice data check, sample text, install data) the way Google and Samsung's engines do — through 1.9 nothing answered those probes, and Nova never appeared in the Preferred engine lists. The app's top line now shows version 2.0 so you can confirm the update landed.

apps.name: Nova Phone
apps.whats_new: New in 1.8 — the agent brain borrows the Gemini key from the Nova Launcher. Nova Phone was the one app that never had borrowing at all, which is why it demanded its own paste. Now: if you've pasted a key into Nova Phone itself it still wins, otherwise she borrows the Launcher's key automatically and refreshes it whenever it changes there. If borrowing fails, the brain's failure line says so with the plain reason. After updating, re-set Nova Phone as your default dialer (Android requires it after an update), and Agent Mode can stay on — no key paste needed if the Launcher has yours.

apps.name: Nova Chat
apps.whats_new: Fixes the blank screen — the app now actually shows the Watch List and Chat Reader.

apps.name: Nova Stream
apps.whats_new: Stream from the phone with RTMP — Twitch and YouTube starter buttons.

apps.name: UHC Claim Builder
apps.whats_new: Signature guaranteed: the form always prints your name as the signature with today's date beside it, the package-ready message reads the signature and date back to you before you send, and if your name is ever blank the package refuses to build instead of producing an unsigned form. New: a Send a test email button on the Build a Claim tab — it sends one clearly marked test email to UHC through your saved Gmail sign-in (no claim attached, no member ID) and, if it fails, shows the mail server's actual words so the problem names itself.

apps.name: Fanciful Companion
apps.whats_new: New in 1.5 — Nova can borrow the Gemini key from the Nova Launcher again. Same root cause as House Log: the app was missing a declaration Android 11+ requires before it may see the Launcher's key service, so the borrow failed silently every time and you had to paste the key here too. The declaration is in, a borrowed key now refreshes from the Launcher instead of being cached forever, and if a borrow ever fails, Nova's heads-up line says why in plain words.

apps.name: Nova House Log
apps.whats_new: New in 1.18 — the camera check's Gemini key borrow actually works now. The borrow code was right, but the app was missing a declaration Android 11+ requires before one app may even SEE another app's key service — so every borrow failed silently and the app just said 'no key'. That declaration is in. Also fixed everywhere in the suite: a borrowed key used to be cached once and kept forever, even after the key changed in the Launcher — now House Log re-borrows on every check, so the Launcher's current key is always the one used. And if borrowing ever fails, the error now says that, with the plain reason, instead of a bare 'no key'. If you pasted a key into House Log itself, yours still wins and is never overwritten.

apps.name: Nova Devotion
apps.whats_new: First release: a daily devotion on your phone — today's verse and reflection spoken in Nova's voice, all 14 banked devotions by ear, and a morning reminder if you want one.

apps.name: Pastor Nova
apps.whats_new: New in 1.17 — key borrowing hardened. The borrow was already working here; what this fixes is the quiet flaw behind it: a borrowed key was cached once and kept forever, so if the key changed in the Launcher, Pastor Nova would have kept preaching on the old copy until it died. Now a borrowed key refreshes from the Launcher every time, a key you paste here yourself still wins, and if a borrow ever fails, the message says why in plain words.

apps.name: Nova Music
apps.whats_new: New in 1.1 — key borrowing hardened. The borrow worked, but the first borrowed key was cached and kept forever — a key changed in the Launcher would never have refreshed here. Now Nova Music re-borrows on every use, and if a borrow fails, the error says that with the plain reason.

apps.name: Nova Bible
apps.whats_new: New in 1.2 — key borrowing hardened. Commentary and Find borrow the key from the Nova Launcher, and that worked — but the first borrowed key was cached and kept forever, so a key changed in the Launcher would never have refreshed here. Now the Bible re-borrows on every use, and if a borrow fails, the message says why in plain words. Reading the text itself never needed the key and still doesn't.

apps.name: Nova RD
apps.whats_new: New in 1.13 — key borrowing hardened. RD only ever borrows (it has no paste of its own), and the borrow worked — but the first borrowed key was cached and treated as RD's own forever, so a key changed in the Launcher never refreshed here. Now RD re-borrows on every use, and if a borrow fails, the error says that with the plain reason. If Google ever rejects the key itself, RD drops its cached copy and borrows fresh next time.

apps.name: Nova Music Therapist
apps.whats_new: New in 1.1 — key borrowing hardened. The borrow itself was built right in 1.0, but a borrowed key was cached once and kept forever — if the key ever changed in the Launcher, this app would have kept using the old copy and failed without saying why. Now a borrowed key refreshes from the Launcher on every session, a key you paste here yourself still wins, and if borrowing ever fails, the failure line says exactly that with the plain reason — never a quota claim Google didn't make. (For the record: the quota error you heard earlier today came from the Launcher itself, and Launcher 3.51 rebuilds that walk — this app never made that call.)
